text:
julian: FYI — customer reported a sudden spike of 502s hitting Hosted API around 09:12 UTC. They see TLS handshake timeouts from our edge and then 502s from custapi. Started right after our cert rotation window.
nana: grabbing logs now. can you paste the customer request-id?
julian: req-id = req_01H2Z4X8, customer says it affects a handful of IPs / ISPs only (multi-region). Sample curl shows TLS alert: 
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/complete -H "Authorization: Bearer x" --resolve api.redwood.example:443:198.51.100.7
* Connected to api.redwood.example (198.51.100.7) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* (tls handshake) SSL_read: Connection reset by peer
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_read: Connection reset by peer, errno 54
```
ryan: interesting — connection reset during TLS post-handshake. can you run openssl s_client with -msg -debug and also dig +trace from the affected IP? suspect resolver returning different A records mid-handshake.
nana: ran a rapid nslookup loop from repro host, saw A records flip between 198.51.100.7 and 203.0.113.9 with TTL 60. Also a small subset returned 0.0.0.0 briefly. pasted trace: 
```
; <<>> DiG 9.10.6 <<>> api.redwood.example @8.8.8.8
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.example.  60 IN A 198.51.100.7
api.redwood.example.  60 IN A 203.0.113.9
```
linda: 0.0.0.0 responses usually indicate our resolver returning SERVFAIL mapped or an upstream hijack. any recent changes to egress NAT pools or egress resolver configs during the cert push?
infra-bot: deploy:cert-rotation v2026.03.17 completed at 09:05 UTC. No egress config changes recorded in the same window.
kyle: I see a correlated spike in resolver timeout errors in the same window 09:10-09:20 UTC from our resolver fleet — increased retransmits to upstream (ASNs 64496/64497). Might be packet loss on the peering path causing resolver retries and inconsistent answers.
ryan: that can cause clients to switch IP mid-handshake if DNS lookup is reissued by client lib after a timeout. If the first IP gets to TLS server with new cert chain and second IP is a different gateway without matching config, handshake can fail. hypothesis: transient resolver/peering packet loss during cert rotation -> client retries with different A -> handshake reset.
nana: confirmed one of the A IPs (203.0.113.9) is a newly warmed gateway with updated cert bundle; other (198.51.100.7) still on older cache for a fraction of requests due to staggered push; mismatch window narrow but matches outage window.
julian: customer wants mitigation and repro steps. they want to know if this will recur on future rotations.
ryan: immediate mitigation: add sticky DNS TTL via traffic router for the next 15m for affected zones, and temporarily route traffic from problematic ISPs away from gateway 198.51.100.7. long term: ensure cert rollout and edge pool update are tightly coupled with DNS updates — avoid exposing both old and new certs to same DNS round-robin during low TTL windows.
linda: creating a short-lived policy now to reduce DNS rotation for api.redwood.example for 30 minutes. also opening communication with peering ops to investigate packetloss to upstream resolvers.
kyle: repro steps for support to capture if customer sees again: 1) from customer IP run: 
```
for i in {1..20}; do dig +short api.redwood.example @<their-resolver> && sleep 2; done
openssl s_client -connect $(dig +short api.redwood.example | head -n1):443 -servername api.redwood.example -msg -debug
```
nana: logging these steps on the escalation ticket and will provide the customer a short post-mortem. also recommending client-side backoff + reuse of existing socket if possible to avoid re-resolving mid-handshake.
julian: thanks — please add a note to the incident channel when the temporary DNS stickiness is live. tagging @ryan for follow-up on rollout playbook changes. :thumbsup:
